contribution_after.assessment: The paper remains a useful synthesis rather than a new result. The revision repairs the formal definition, aligns its normative admissibility filter, drops the distorted extreme-tail survey ratio and capability-theory mischaracterization, integrates the missing bioethics/disability/empirical literature including Blackiston and Levin (2013), and adds non-bodily regulation comparisons. However, Propositions 1-3 remain straightforward set-theoretic consequences of a conjunctive path definition with no empirical measurement of the four-layer framework carried out, and the Pew analysis remains an unadjusted bivariate comparison of published aggregates on excitement and generic regulation preferences because the respondent-level Wave 99 microdata are behind a Pew account gate.

summary: Round 1 closes 11 of the 12 findings from REVIEW/findings-hydrogen.json and leaves hydrogen:F4 partially closed (the misleading extreme-tail ratio was removed and adjacent steps and group coverages were added, while Pew ATP Wave 99 respondent-level data require a Pew account and remain unmodeled, leaving party-religiosity confounding unadjusted in bivariate tables). All 44 prose quantity numerals are bound in claims.yaml and match the verified simulation results and Pew PDFs; the 9 new references match registry records; the visual build of 21 pages is clean aside from a minor split definition lead-in across pages 5-6; and the paper represents a useful synthesis.
